Hi Amy — thanks for the clear ask.

High level plan (summary):
- Run two benchmark phases over 48 hours: steady-state profiling (low-to-medium concurrency) and surge/saturation window (step up concurrency to 100+ to observe degradation modes).
- Primary metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token) for streaming generation, per-token streaming latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end request latency, and throughput (tokens/sec).
- Workloads: 3 prompt families representative of your clinical note flows: short prompt (~30 tokens), context-heavy (~600 token context + 300 token generation), and multi-turn chat (10-turn session).
- Acceptance criteria for MAP: p95 TTFT < 250ms at 30 concurrent users for short prompts; graceful degradation with 90% requests <= p99 threshold during surge window (detailed below).

I'll attach the run plan and the scripts we will execute. Proposed ETA for the initial report with raw CSVs is EOD Nov 15 (5 business days from now). If that timeline works, we'll schedule a small kickoff with your SRE on Thursday to validate network egress and keys.

Next steps:
1) Confirm target concurrency and any blocked IPs for test traffic.
2) Share any sample prompts you want included (recommend at least 20 presence of clinical terms).
3) Confirm acceptance thresholds (we proposed p95 TTFT 250ms for short prompts).

Thanks — tagging Marcus for the bench run and Vanessa for account next steps.

— Jasmine Liu

Thanks — I reviewed the scripts. Technical notes for the run:
- We'll use a client that mimics your browser streaming (chunked SSE) so TTFT captures server first-token emission + network RTT.
- Test harness config: 3 phases — ramp (0->30 users in 5m), steady (30m at X users), surge (step to 60, 100 users, hold 5m each) and cooldown.
- Metrics we will collect server-side: first_token_timestamp, each_chunk_latency, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization, host-level network p95/99.
- We'll run each workload 5 times and report median per-run plus combined p50/p95/p99.
- Important: We will test with and without KV prefix caching enabled; caching typically reduces TTFT for multi-turn by 30–60% depending on context length.

I also added a short checklist for provable acceptance:
- p95 TTFT <= 250ms for short prompt at 30 concurrency
- p95 per-token streaming latency <= 120ms at 30 concurrency
- No sustained GPU OOMs or retriable rate-limit errors during surge window
- Error budget: <1% 5xx across surge window

I'll coordinate a run Friday morning PST unless you prefer Monday.

— Marcus

Run started at 07:30 PST. Short log highlights (live):
- Phase 1 (ramp): clean, no 5xx, p50 TTFT for short prompt ~110ms.
- Phase 2 (steady at 30): p95 TTFT ~230ms, p95 per-token latency ~95ms, GPU utilization 62%. KV cache not enabled for first pass.
- Surge step to 90 concurrent (hold 90s): observed p99 TTFT spike to 1.6s for long-context prompts; short prompts remained within 600ms p99. A portion of requests hit transient 429s due to our test harness hitting a client-side limiter — we throttled and re-ran the step.

Subject: Final findings and MAP entry — streaming surge evaluation (p50/p95/p99)

Amy/Peyton — attaching the final report + one-page acceptance summary. Key findings and MAP entries below (short summary for procurement):

One-page acceptance summary (pass/fail):
- p95 TTFT <= 250ms at 30 concurrency (short prompts): PASS (measured p95 = 225ms, KV-disabled).
- p95 per-token streaming latency <= 120ms at 30 concurrency: PASS (measured p95 = 98ms).
- No sustained GPU OOMs or retriable infra errors during surge window: PASS (no OOMs; transient 429s attributable to client-side limiter during a synthetic surge step, not server-side enforcement).
- Error budget <1% 5xx across surge: PASS (measured 0.2% 5xx).

Detailed observations:
- KV prefix caching (enabled in second pass) reduced p95 TTFT for multi-turn scenarios by ~38% (long-context test went from p95 780ms -> 480ms). This is recommended as part of production config for multi-turn clinical dialogs.
- Surge behavior: under the abrupt 3x short surge, p99 TTFT for long-context prompts crossed 1.5s in the initial run; after tuning request queuing (small increase to request queue depth) and enabling per-route fallback to a smaller model variant, tail latency stabilized.
- Concurrency recommendations: for cost/latency balance, we recommend reserving Dedicated capacity with burst policy to handle predictable EHR-sync spikes.

MAP action items and owners (for your MAP):
- Runbook: add a 3-step surge mitigation runbook to MAP — owner: TIA SRE (Peyton) / Redwood ops (Sergio) — due Nov 23.
- Config: enable KV prefix caching by default for chat route — owner: TIA engineering / Redwood solutions — due Nov 19.
- SLA addendum: include performance snapshot in contract addendum, reference csv and traces stored in shared Drive HS-7842 — owner: Vanessa — due Nov 18.

Attached: full CSVs of raw runs, sample trace, bench scripts, and MAP-v1.3 with updated milestones. Let me know if you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough this week.

Thanks — excited to close this out.

— Jasmine Liu
